# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (5-, 8-, 13-, 21-, 34-, 55-period) compresses to unusually low width relative to ATR, indicating reduced volatility and equilibrium, a subsequent break below the compression candle's low on expanding volume often triggers a short-term mean-reversion move downward. This setup captures asymmetric short-side momentum during elevated volatility regimes (VIX > 18) when compression breakouts are more likely to fail and reverse.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** Calculate ribbon width as \|21-EMA - 55-EMA\| on 5-minute bars. If ribbon width < 0.25×ATR(14) for three consecutive bars and the current bar closes below the low of the widest compression bar within that window with volume > 2× the 20-bar average volume, go short at the close.  
**Exit:** Initial stop at the highest high during the compression window (the compression candle's high). Target at 1.5R (risk-reward). After hitting target, trail the remaining half position with a 12% ATR chandelier exit (using ATR(14) multiplied by 0.12, subtracted from the highest high since entry).  
**Regime filters:** Only active when VIX > 18 (to avoid low-VIX chop) and between 10:30-14:00 ET (midday when compression breakouts are more likely to reverse). Disabled when VIX < 12.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account ~= 14% of headline P&L (scales linearly with contracts).  
2. **Sample bias:** Zero-sample proposal; idea derived from price action observation and volatility regime logic. High overfit risk due to no historical validation; requires rigorous out-of-sample testing to avoid curve-fitting to recent volatility regimes.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward or held-out window tested).  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic bid/ask/slippage simulation on anchor days).  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: whipsaw in low-VIX (<12) chop causing repeated stops; max drawdown scenario: consecutive failing breakouts during VIX contraction; blow-up scenario: volatility expansion triggering stop runs during news events (FOMC/CPI) when compression breaks fail to reverse.  
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (if top-5 days drive >60% of P&L, strategy is regime-fragile).
